- **objectui#11005's ACCEPT and landing (03:2xZ).** The landing ops went out in the same script as the ACCEPT, ungated on its exit code; the ACCEPT was refused on a stamp-contract check (a test-case instant written as a timestamp) and posted a minute later, before the merge, naming the slip (`5883018877`). Lesson: a landing is sent only after the ACCEPT's post exits 0.
- **objectui#10964's claim (03:2xZ to 03:35Z).** The label write was the 40th write of the hour and the claim the 41st, refused by write-pace; the card sat labelled and assigned with no claim for about ten minutes, until the window reopened. Lesson: the 40-an-hour budget is shared by every agent in this container, so read `write-pace.mjs --status` before a claim pair and start none that cannot finish.
- **objectui#10982's claim (04:35Z).** Its serial line read objectui#10993's in-flight surface from that card's claim, not from its pushed branch, which already edited `packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` (the `form.title` / `form.description` read, outside that claim's surface). The hunks are disjoint (`:69`, `:985`, `:2480` against `:1206` and the non-grid loading state); both devs were told, and the one that lands second merges `main`. Lesson: read an in-flight card's surface from its branch's three-dot diff, not from its claim.
- **objectui#11002's dispatch (05:58Z).** The order assumed `ConsoleShell` gates on `useDiscovery()`; the dev measured that false and found no advertised signal at all, and stopped at the order's valve with nothing changed. The seat escalated the card instead of dispatching a second time.
- **The write budget.** Four ACCEPT pairs, five cards and two claims in one hour held the shared 40-an-hour token at the ceiling twice (06:29Z, 06:41Z). Landing now runs through budget-gated scripts that post each ACCEPT and its landing ops as a pair only when two slots are free, gate the landing on the ACCEPT's exit code, and hold every card number until the board shows it.

- **Container restart (about 00:01Z, 2026-09-30).** The restart killed two dev subagents (objectui#11148, objectui#11145) mid-verification, and the two merge watchers. No write was lost: both devs had pushed, objectui#11080's ACCEPT had posted (`5901343062`), and both PRs were already in the merge queue. The devs were resumed from their transcripts and the watchers re-armed.
- **An unexplained merge-queue hang (02:23Z).** PR objectui#11164's first merge group hung in `Test (shard 8/8)` until its 20-minute job timeout, and the job log is unrecoverable (blob 404). The dev's patch round (`5903675431`) did not reproduce it: the exact merge tree's shard 8 passed twice, and the PR's pins hash into other shards. The seat re-queued it once, unchanged (`5903691501`), and it passed. It is recorded as unexplained, not as a flake. The CI keeps no per-file trace of a stalled shard. A progress reporter is a `ci.yml` change for the maintainer or the gate lane, and it is not filed.

## 4. Notes (durable)

- `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr N` and `dispatch-gates.mjs` gate families answer only for objectstack. For objectui, derive the path surface from the PR's file list; the tier half answers with `--tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectui`.
- Several `domain:ui` seats are live at once. Re-read open-PR file lists and live claims before every claim; the board moves in minutes.
- `git fetch A B` sets `FETCH_HEAD` to the first ref: fetch into a named ref for any `merge-tree` probe. Judge a PR by three-dot diff or its file list.
- `objectstack-ai/cloud` is unreachable from these sessions; cloud-contract cards carry that as a declared reading gap.
- objectui squash-merges with the PR title and body, and GitHub appends every squashed commit's `Co-authored-by` trailer. A pushed commit that carries a model identifier means moving the change to a fresh branch, because force-push is barred.
- Every write goes through `scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs`, `label-write.mjs` or the fleet relay; the budget is 40 writes an hour per token, and every agent in this container spends the same token (devs' PR, assignee and report writes included). Read `node scripts/pm/write-pace.mjs --status` before a batch.
- **`Fixes #N` does not close the card on objectui's merge-queue merges.** It was observed twice on 2026-09-30: objectui#9830 and objectui#11158 were both still open minutes after the merge, with no `closed` event on the timeline. The seat closes a `Fixes` card itself after verifying by content, with a close note, `state_reason: completed`.
- A job log is read through the MCP `get_job_logs` tool; the REST log URL redirects to blob storage the proxy refuses. A failed job is re-run with MCP `rerun_failed_jobs` (REST answers 403).
- **Director reminder `5903848327`** (2026-09-30): a contract-review record covers the landing head. Re-record after any base merge, regeneration or changeset-prose edit; the one exception is a `Regen-provenance:` line. A review face owes a record whatever `Clause-②` says. Apply it at every enqueue.
- **Cross-lane memos.**
  - objectstack-ai/objectstack#20758 (the `breadcrumb` spec retirement): the objectui pin-bump PR that installs it must drop the `breadcrumb` input from `page:header`'s registration, and the "accepts it until objectstack#20758 retires it" sentence in `content/docs/layout/page-header.mdx` and `content/docs/guide/layout.md`. `nav:breadcrumb` is registered only as `placeholders.tsx`'s scaffold (PR objectui#11172's review `5904304282`).
  - objectui#11165 (the slotted-pages header example) is `domain:devx`.
